title.narrative: Power to Youth Ghana

description.narrative: Power to You(th) is a five-year program from 2021 - 2025, the Power to You(th) programme (PTY) will empower adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) to increase their agency, claim their rights, address gender inequalities, challenge gender norms, and advocate for inclusive decision-making. As a result, harmful practices such as female genital mutilation/ cutting (FGM/C) and child marriage (CM), sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), and unintended pregnancies will be decreased

title.narrative: PATHWAY 2: Strengthening civil society

description.narrative: CSOs amplify young peoples voices to claim, protect and expand civic space

title.narrative: Description of effective use of accountability mechanisms by citizens/communities and CSOs towards SRHR of all people (SRHR I)

comment.narrative: Most harmful practices are discussed in community sessions with the notion to protect members of the community. Community leaders do not promote or foster social accountability. Despite the efforts of CSOs, there is no visible results to account for lobby and advocacy efforts

In 2021 there were no accountability activities to address this target. The year 2021 was to have a clear understanding of the state of SRHR issues within the communities, have social actors commit to having some actions around that and thus set action plans to addressing SRHR issues to serve as a benchmark for accountability of duty bearers. At the state actor level, year one served as evidence gathering to engage state actors to account for their stewardship.
CSOs aligned to the standard operating protocols within the non profit organization Secretariat

Over the period, through the CSOs learning hub initiative and the youth initiative small grant model, about 16 grassroot organizations (youth led and youth focused) were supported with technical assisstance and financial as well to enable them align with the SOP for non profit organization. A notable one is the Girls Adviosry Council.
Young people undertake accountability activities to hold duty bearers accountable

The 2023 FY witnessed the youth PMEL, AGYWs and other members of the MoYs engaged the parliamentarians of the Northern zone of Ghana on issues of sanitary pads and sexual and gender-based violence within the communities under their constituents.
No target was set for 2022.

Though not planned as part of activities, AGWYs within the year 2022 took personal initiative to hold duty bearers accountable. They employed follow up dialogue meetings and participation in state actors meeting to demand the address of issues affecting them. A key area that saw AGYWs act around was the quest to have 20% levy on sanitary pads removed. AGYWs used street match, reading and submissions of pertitions and series of follow up visits to push the govenrment throught the Northern Regional coordination council to act by removing the levy. The approach also saw a joint CSOs action to amplify youth voices by the engagement of some parliamentarians to among other items push for a repeal of the tax on sanitary pads.

comment.narrative: 50 were undertaken at the community level while 22 were undertaken at the Regional and National level. TV, Radio , Social media and face-to-face approaches were employed in carrying out our advocacy initiatives over the period under review. This exceeds the 50 that was targeted and this is due to some review of strategies of rollout and the operationalization of the YISG initiative.

The CSOs in the learning hub were asked to develop a yearly workplans. These workplans highlighted the advocacy initiatives they will be undertaking on quarterly basis. Upon further follow-up with the members of the CSOs learning hub it was realized that several members had taken significant initiatives within their immediate surroundings

Social media advocacy was carried out by the CMT for World Contraceptive Day, Safe Abortion and 16 Days of Activism. title.narrative: # of times government or private sector at all levels include CSOs in decision making processes related to our advocacy issues, react to CSO positions by adopting their argumentation, or putting our advocacy issues on the agenda

comment.narrative: In 2024, the programme leveraged on the 2024 presidential and parliamentary elections to lobby for the inclusion of key PTY issues be adopted in their manisfestos. It is worth highlighting that, the two polical parties manisfesto committes, engaged with CSOs, including PTY on youth related issues to be considered in their manisfestos. This presented the Ghana consortium with an opprtunity to advocate for the effective implementation of the youth policy. Again, the programme was also invited to participate in a number of meetings and decison making discussions by the ministry of gender, children and social protection and the parliament of Ghana. Some of these meetings were; stakeholders meeting on the update of the operational monitoring and evaluation plan on ending child marriage (2023-2024), validation of the child marriage study and the speaker of parliament's yearly planning meetings respectively. These engagement presented the consortium with an opportunity to advocate."

The CMT recorded 11 inclusions or invitation both in the quest to making key decisions as well as to engage on issues relating to the power To Youth agenda of addressing affecting young people especially AGYWs.
Underachievement because 2021 did not see the inclusion of the CMT of PtY in some advocacy decisions.

title.narrative: PATHWAY 3: Changing social norms

description.narrative: Societal actors support and promote youth rights and progressive social norms

title.narrative: # of media reports on PtY key issues that influence public and political debate

comment.narrative: 12 Radio (2 at National Level and 10 at the District level) and 1 TV - GTV breakfast show (National broadcaster)
The programme held a number of twitter storms, strategic engagements on X space, media engagements(radio, tv ) as part of the commemoration of key international days.

These reports were recorded across online publications, radio discussions and social media handles. Some programme intervention outcomes were pickup and published online, for instance the recuse of a Junior high School graduate who has adducted for marriage by man within the Kayoro community and was rescued with the help of LLVs became a talk of town. Also, media sessions triggered a lot of discussions from radio listeners, social media followers on Facebook and twitter on the topical issues Pty seeks to address.

title.narrative: Level of public support for family planning and prevention of harmful practices and SGBV

comment.narrative: In 2021 there were no activities on Family planning component for this target, because CMT Ghana is focusing on community entry and stakeholder mapping to inform further programming. In the area of support for the prevention of harmful practices and SGBV, some communities through their leaders have given their support to ending these issues. They raised some of these as issues bedeviling their communities and thus need to be addressed to create a friendly and open space for progressive development. Some opinion leaders such as chiefs gave assurance of putting in place to address the issues child marriage, unintended pregnancies and SGBV. Some communities had conventional ways of attending to the issues of unintended pregnancies where elders refuse to attend the naming ceremony of babies conceived out of wedlock.
about 8 communities buy into family planing and contraceptive use and 15 communities have bylaws to address harmful practices by end of 2023

Many activities have been implemented on family planning, harmful practices and Sexual and Gender-Based Violence. This has led to the gradual acceptance and support leading to the establishment of community byelaws to protect AGYW from harmful practices. Most communities are now demonstrating a moderate acceptance of family planning with a notable emphasis on preventing SGBV and harmful practices. The decisions of traditional authorities to include young women in decision making signifies a promising step forward in promoting a more inclusive and informed approach to family planning within communities. Despite the improvement observed, work is still ongoing as there still exist a lot myths surrounding reproductive health.
Commitment of chiefs to put in place by-laws to addressing HP, UP and SGBV

There has been a limited but gradual improvement in the support from the Pty communities for family planning programmes. There are still a lot of myths surrounding family planning which needs much more dialogues and sensitization of men to improve the situation. This is from some side conversations with some members from communities. But as a programme, 2023 will see the rollout of FP advocacy as the first years were to get community buy-in for the programme before FP rollout. On the part of community support for the prevention of harmful practices and SGBV, all 40 communities are responsive to the call of ending harmful practices and SGBV from their communities. This is seen in the corporation and support given to Legal Literacy volunteers working within the community as well as the desires of communities to draft bye-laws to curtail the practices. Some communities are far advanced with the process, with some by-laws under review for gazzetting (Kayoro community) and others awaiting the gazetting process (Sirigu Community). Bayanwaya, Yerokoi and Nkanchina No. 2 communities are currently drafting their bylaws with the goal of going through the gazetting process
About 20 communities buy into family planning and contraceptive use and 15 communities have bylaws to address harmful practises by end of 2024

Through male engagement on family planning and the monthly health rallies activities, the PtY program has broken the acceptance barrier of family planning information in about 30 out of 40 communities within the programme. Aside engaging with communities directly on the myths around family planning and the need to accept this as a safe practice, the initiative also successfully triggered the community health services to replicate a similar sensitization efforts in both PTY and non pty communities, leading to greater impact and acceptance.Also, the focus of two of the YISG grantees( Sawla Model Girls Alumni and the Visionary Buluk foundation) integrated family planning into their advocacy. They orgnised intergenerational dialogue meetings between young people and the community elders to hold these conversations. This led to the positive atitudes of community leaders towrds accepting planning planning.

title.narrative: PATHWAY 4: Policies and policy implementation

description.narrative: State actors improve policymaking and implementation on key issues

title.narrative: # of (inter)national laws, policies, norms and practices implemented to decrease barriers to SRHR and prevent harmful practices, and SGBV (SCS 1)

comment.narrative: Multiple laws and policies protect youth rights in Ghana, however there are implementationchallenges at the local level. At community level, advocating for child rights can be considered asencouraging children to be disrespectful to their elders. By-laws are more respected than nationallaws but implementation depends on local leaders and their ability to command respect/adherencefrom communities. Some participants mentioned positive changes through certain policies suchas the Child and Family Welfare Policy 2015, the Children Act Amendment (2018) and the GhanaNational Social Protection Policy (2015). Participants felt government agencies were not doingenough to educate the public on laws & policies. Participants reported that policy reviews andimplementation largely depend on external funding from development partners.
This was due to the limited space of implementation in the first year of the programme.

title.narrative: # and type of (inter)national laws and policies blocked, adopted, maintained, improved including the number of detrimental policies which are prevented or blocked from adoption or development to decrease barriers to SRHR and prevent harmful practices and SGBV (SCS 2, SRHR H)

comment.narrative: Through efforts of United Nations via meetingsof experts on violence against women, therehave been conscious steps taken to bringgovernment’s attention and actions on theSRHR issues in Ghana. These engagementshave produced international agreementsor treaties. The baseline study identified 21international agreements or treaties, and thesehave informed the promulgation of13 anti-SGBVlaws in Ghana, though it was found out that somecommunity members have no knowledge of theexistence of these international agreements ortreaties. And the implementation of these alsoshows a lot of space for improvement.

In 2023, the PTY Ghana programme partnered with the SDGs platform to carry out a campaign against the imposition of the 15% luxury tax on sanitary products which got the attention of the speaker of parliament of Ghana, Mr. Alban Bagbin to speak on the issue. He desvribed the act as a "cardinal sin" during parliamentary proceedings on 22nd June 2023. Fast forwward on 5th November, 2023, during the 2024 budgt reading in parliament, the fnance minister had announce that the government had removed all taxes on raw materials used to produced sanitary pads locally. This move aimed to reduce the financal burden of menstrual hygine for Ghanaian women and the AGYW.

The program could not influence the review of the adolescent reproductive health guidelines due the ongoing anti-LGBTQ+ bill in parliament. This bill has led to the misconception about SRHR which has made engagements with stakeholders slow. Some stakeholders do not even want to engage in conversations around it.

This could not be realised as the program could not influence the review of the adolescent reproductive health guideline as was targeted. But stakeholders have been engaged with knowlegde product (policy brief) as a trigger to the broader conversation as an initial step.
This was due to the limited space of implementation in the first year of the programme.

title.narrative: # of (inter)national laws, policies, norms and practices implemented to decrease barriers to SRHR and prevent harmful practices, and SGBV (SCS 1)

comment.narrative: 10 community leaders, Gutaa, Dohani, Lungni, Kpalori, Mantana, Temaa, Balenrinsa, Kunyigsa,Yerikoi and Bupei communities have out in place directives to address issues of SGBV and harmful practices such as forced and exchange marriages, widowhood rite and teenage pregnancies within their communities. Al though these directives have not been documented or gazetted (legalized to become laws) but they have contributed to reducing these key issues in their communities. For instance, Gutaa and Mantana reported zero child marriage and teenage pregnancies since the directives were put in place in 2023.

5 community laws have been drafted (Sirigu and Kayoro communities) and are currently drafting bylaws (Bayanwaya, Yerikoi, and Nkanchina no.2). Some laws which will be included in the draft bylaws have been communicated verbally to communities and thus in action awaiting the formalization of the provisions. This includes the indefinite ban on night social gatherings which contributes to unintended pregnancies, especially in the case of young people and also, the prohibition of marriage by abduction.

The program was not able to meet the target of having 15 community by-laws. However, we able to help most of the communities to gazette (made a law) the by-laws that were drafted in 2022. The 4 by-laws includes those related to criminalising early marriage and other harmful practices in communities.

title.narrative: Whether or not legal frameworks are in place to promote, enforce, implement and monitor equality and non-discrimination on the basis of sex

comment.narrative: 10 community leaders, Gutaa, Dohani, Lungni, Kpalori, Mantana, Temaa, Balenrinsa, Kunyigsa,Yerikoi and Bupei communities have out in place directives to address issues of SGBV and harmful practices such as forced and exchange marriages, widowhood rite and teenage pregnancies within their communities. Al though these directives have not been documented or gazetted (legalized to become laws) but they have contributed to reducing these key issues in their communities.
Communities put in place measures to sustain the fight against issues of SGBV, harmful practices and unintended pregnancies such as addreesing retrogressive social norms

In 2022, most communities had started drafting bye-laws to addressing the 3 key issues PTY seek to address. In 2023, the communities had moved from drafting to gazetting the bye-laws. An example is the Sirigu traditional council lunched their bye-laws on teenage pregnancy and some harmful practices to take effect immidiatly.

In Ghana, Communities through their traditional authorities have translated their commits as was revorded in 2021 to drafting community by-laws to addressing the 3 key issues PtY seeks to address. Some communities are progressing from the drafting stage to the gazzetting stage which will give legal backing to the by-laws and thus its full implementation.

Traditional and religious leaders have increased their commitment to support in the advocacy to promote eradication of SGBV issues affecting AGYW through making pronouncements in their various jurisdictions in all 40 communities. The community members have also increased their commitment to address HPs including facilitating the reporting of SHBV issues to support its eradication in communities. Some Media personnel made commitment their support to the PtY programme to fight against the key issues

title.narrative: PATHWAY 1: Strengthening youth to claim civic space

description.narrative: Young people demand accountability and responsiveness on key issues

title.narrative: # of young people who participate in policy and decision-making bodies and perceive their participation as meaningful (SRHR A)

comment.narrative: The programme overachieved the target by 213% due to opportunity created by 2024 presidential and parliamentary elections and the Youth talk Initiative. The elections meant policymakers were willing to hear the concerns of the population (including young people). PtY supported Youth advocates to engage with their MPs in an activity called "Ask your MPs" to discuss their main policy agenda and manifestos in order to lobby for the integration of youth concerns and issues especially around the key issues. This led to 4 MPs adopting portions of the Youth policy into their manifesto and also committing to using part of the MPs common fund to address issues around SGBVs and Harmful practices within their constituencies. PtY also supported the participation of young people in the review of the child marriage framework to reflect the current realities of young people.In addition, the Youth talk initiative facilitated the Youth talk member participation in town/area council meetings, budget review meeting and general assembly meetings to discusses the district level policies and initiatives.Lastly, the YISG grantee, Centre for Contemporary Pan Africanism(CCPA) created the "Youth council for gender responsive policies". The youth council engaged the ministry of gender, children and social protection in a dialogue meeting to facilitate the implementation of gender responsive policies.

The role out of the YISG initiatives broadened the reach and thus the over-achievement. Activities rollout by these grantees focused primarily on the youth, specifically AGYWs at the centre of their interventions. This included the quest to bring young people to the decision table across all levels (community, District, and regional levels). The achieved of 149 is broken down as 95 young females54 young males.

The second phase of YISG scaled up from 10 grantees in the first phase to 13 grantees in the second phase. This increment led to the rollout of more youth activities. Most of the activities were directed to the inclusion of young people in decision making across all levels(communities, District and regional levels). These activities led to the inclusion of more young people in decision making platforms espercially at the community level( traditional councils)

These young people participated in the inception meetings with the district assembly officials to make a decision on the choice of communities. Underachievement was due to the limited period of programme implementation.

title.narrative: # of youth advocates with an improved understanding of decision-making processes and power dynamics regarding key topics

comment.narrative: The Youthatalk initiave which was focused on youth participation in local governance, created room for the engagement of more young people in understanding the decision making spaces and power dynamics around the key issues. Also, at the community level, there has been increased engagement or involvememt of young people in traditional decision making spaces as part of efforts to amplify youth voices in key decision making spaces. Lastly, this year's YISG was largely on promoting youth voices in decision making spaces at community, district, regional and National level, especially on areas such as family planning, SGBV and community development. These strategies contributed to the 151% overachievement of the target.
